title: "Plot MSE Multiple Lines"
author: "Santiago Morante"

  html_document:
    keep_md: yes
---

This file is intended to plot the Mean Square Error generated during a experiment (frame by frame). It is expected that you have 3 files for different alpha and beta parameters.

To correctly see the plot, first set the working directory (change the next path to the one you want).

```{r}
setwd("../results")
```

Next, introduce the name of the files containing the MSE of your training experiment.

```{r}
filename_training_1 = "motion_results_07.Apr.2015_13:35:33.csv"
filename_training_2 = "motion_results_07.Apr.2015_13:35:33.csv"
filename_training_3 = "motion_results_07.Apr.2015_13:35:33.csv"
```

Next, introduce the name of the files containing the MSE of your test experiment. They must be in the same order than the training files.

```{r}
filename_test_1 = "motion_results_07.Apr.2015_14:28:42.csv"
filename_test_2 = "motion_results_07.Apr.2015_14:28:42.csv"
filename_test_3 = "motion_results_07.Apr.2015_14:28:42.csv"

```

Now we define the types of lines and their colors. Also we define other parameters of the plot.

```{r}

# line type: http://www.cookbook-r.com/Graphs/Shapes_and_line_types/
type_line_1=1
type_line_2=3
type_line_3=5

# line colors: http://www.stat.columbia.edu/~tzheng/files/Rcolor.pdf
color_line_1= 'dodgerblue4'
color_line_2= 'black'
color_line_3= 'darkgoldenrod1'

# line width
width = 3

# rectangle transparency
alpha_channel=0.08

```


That's all you need to you. If everything went ok, next chunk should show you the plot.

```{r}
data_training_1 = read.csv(filename_training_1, header = TRUE)
data_training_2 = read.csv(filename_training_2, header = TRUE)
data_training_3 = read.csv(filename_training_3, header = TRUE)

data_test_1 = read.csv(filename_test_1, header = TRUE)
data_test_2 = read.csv(filename_test_2, header = TRUE)
data_test_3 = read.csv(filename_test_3, header = TRUE)

# same for the 3 experiments (theoretically)
x_total = 1:(nrow(data_training)+nrow(data_test))

# different for each of the experiments
y_training_1 = as.numeric(data_training_1$Mean.Square.Error)
y_test_1 = as.numeric(data_test_1$Mean.Square.Error)
y_total_1 = c(y_training_1, y_test_1)
y_total_1 = y_total_1 / 255^2 # maximum square error for a single pixel 

y_training_2 = as.numeric(data_training_2$Mean.Square.Error)
y_test_2 = as.numeric(data_test_2$Mean.Square.Error)
y_total_2 = c(y_training_2, y_test_2)
y_total_2 = y_total_2 / 255^2 # maximum square error for a single pixel 

y_training_3 = as.numeric(data_training_3$Mean.Square.Error)
y_test_3 = as.numeric(data_test_3$Mean.Square.Error)
y_total_3 = c(y_training_3, y_test_3)
y_total_3 = y_total_3 / 255^2 # maximum square error for a single pixel 

############# PLOT #########
# declare device
plot(0,0,
     xlim = c(0,nrow(data_training)+nrow(data_test)),
     ylim = c(0,1),
     type = "n",
     xlab = "Frame", ylab = "Normalized Error", main = "Normalized Mean Square Error")

############# plot lines
lines(x_total, y_total_1, 
     type = "l", 
     col = color_line_1, 
     lty = type_line_1, 
     lwd=width)

lines(x_total, y_total_2, 
     type = "l", 
     col = color_line_2,
     lty = type_line_2,
     lwd=width)

lines(x_total, y_total_3, 
     type = "l", 
     col = color_line_3,
     lty = type_line_3,
     lwd=width)

############# plot rectangles
rect(0, 0, nrow(data_training),1,
     border = FALSE, 
     col=rgb(1, 0, 0, alpha=alpha_channel))

rect(nrow(data_training), 0, nrow(data_training)+nrow(data_test),1, 
     border = FALSE, 
     col=rgb(0, 0, 1, alpha=alpha_channel))

############# plot text
text(c(nrow(data_training)/2, (nrow(data_training)+nrow(data_test))/2 ),
     c(0.95,0.95),
     labels=c("Training","Test"),
     font=2,
     family="B",
     col = c("red", "blue"))

############# plot legend
legend('topright',
       c(expression(alpha~"=XX, "~beta~"=XX"), 
         expression(alpha~"=XX, "~beta~"=XX"), 
         expression(alpha~"=XX, "~beta~"=XX")),  
       col=c(color_line_1, color_line_2, color_line_3),
       lty=c(type_line_1, type_line_2, type_line_3),
       lwd=2,
       bty='o', # alternative n 
       cex=.8) #size of legend

```
